mcqs.learning_point: Describe motion using distance and time
mcqs.question: Two cars start from the same point. Car A travels 150 metres in 10 seconds, while Car B travels 200 metres in 20 seconds. Which statement correctly compares their motions using distance and time?

options.A: Car A has a higher speed than Car B.
options.B: Car B has a higher speed than Car A.
options.C: Both cars have the same speed.
options.D: Speed cannot be compared without knowing the acceleration.

mcqs.answer: Car A has a higher speed than Car B.
mcqs.explanation: Speed is distance divided by time. Car A: 150 m / 10 s = 15 m/s. Car B: 200 m / 20 s = 10 m/s. Since 15 m/s > 10 m/s, Car A moves faster. Options B, C, and D are incorrect because they either reverse the comparison, ignore the calculation, or introduce irrelevant information.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify periodic motion in everyday examples
mcqs.question: Which of the following everyday phenomena best exemplifies periodic motion?

options.A: The swinging pendulum of a wall clock.
options.B: A car accelerating on a highway.
options.C: A ball rolling down a slope and coming to rest.
options.D: A leaf falling from a tree.

mcqs.answer: The swinging pendulum of a wall clock.
mcqs.explanation: Periodic motion repeats at regular intervals; a pendulum swings back and forth in a regular cycle. The car accelerating, the ball rolling to rest, and the leaf falling are not repetitive cycles, so options B, C, and D are incorrect.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand motion as change in position
mcqs.question: In physics, motion is best defined as:

options.A: Change in position of an object with respect to time.
options.B: Change in mass of an object.
options.C: Change in color of an object.
options.D: Change in temperature of an object.

mcqs.answer: Change in position of an object with respect to time.
mcqs.explanation: Motion refers to the alteration of an object's location over time. Mass, color, and temperature changes are unrelated to the definition of motion, making options B, C, and D incorrect.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify objects at rest and in motion relative to a reference point
mcqs.question: A book lies on a table while a train passes a stationary platform. Which statement correctly identifies the state of each object relative to the platform?

options.A: The book is at rest and the train is in motion.
options.B: The book is in motion and the train is at rest.

mcqs.answer: The book is at rest and the train is in motion.
mcqs.explanation: Relative to the platform, the book does not change its position, so it is at rest. The train moves past the platform, so it is in motion. Options B, C, and D misidentify the states.

mcqs.question: Which pair correctly matches the type of motion with its description?

options.A: Linear motion – movement along a straight line; Rotational motion – movement around an axis.
options.B: Linear motion – movement around a circle; Rotational motion – movement in a straight line.
options.C: Linear motion – staying still; Rotational motion – moving back and forth.
options.D: Linear motion – random motion; Rotational motion – straight‑line motion.

mcqs.answer: Linear motion – movement along a straight line; Rotational motion – movement around an axis.
mcqs.explanation: Linear motion follows a straight path, while rotational motion involves turning about an axis. Options B, C, and D describe the motions incorrectly.

mcqs.learning_point: Describe motion using distance and time
mcqs.question: A student walks 120 metres in 60 seconds. What is the student's average speed?
mcqs.explanation: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 120 m ÷ 60 s = 2 m/s. Options A, C, and D result from incorrect division.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify periodic motion in everyday examples
mcqs.question: Which of the following examples shows periodic motion?

options.B: A car stopping at a traffic light.
options.C: A person climbing a set of stairs.

mcqs.explanation: A metronome produces regular, repeating beats, a classic case of periodic motion. The other situations occur once or do not repeat regularly, so they are not periodic.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand motion as change in position
mcqs.question: A child moves from point A to point B and then returns to point A. Which statement best describes the child's motion?

options.A: The child changed position twice, showing motion.
options.B: The child remained at the same position overall, so there was no motion.
options.C: Motion only occurs if the child moves in a straight line.
options.D: Motion requires a change in speed, not just a change in position.

mcqs.answer: The child changed position twice, showing motion.
mcqs.explanation: Motion is any change in position. The child first moves away from A to B and then back to A, constituting two changes in position. Options B, C, and D misunderstand the definition of motion.
